actions.action: Cut the woody stalk back to just above a node with green growth (or near soil if no green nodes)
Pinch growing tips above a pair of healthy leaves, taking no more than a third at once
Remove flower buds when they appear
Thin the seedlings, keeping the strongest one
If drooping doesn't recover after watering, inspect the roots
Check soil and water when the top inch is dry
Keep the pot in bright light

reason: The answer's main diagnosis is a woody, improperly pruned basil, and its advice to cut back the stalk and pinch above leaf nodes matches the pruning fix that worked, with nothing harmful.
